paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by a language model before and after instruction tuning, categorized by different types of contact. The horizontal axis displays the contact types: “Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” “Virtual Contact,” “No Contact Before,” and “No Contact After,” arranged in alphabetical order. The vertical axis represents the percentage of biased responses, ranging from 0.00% to 60.00% with a linear scale. The values are labeled numerically, with tick intervals of 10%. The tallest bar, representing “Positive Contact After” for “Support of Authorities,” has a value of 47.28%, while the shortest bar, representing “Positive Contact After” for “Virtual Contact,” has a value of 0.04%. The chart is composed of grouped bars, with each bar divided into two sections representing “Negative Contact Before” (light blue) and “Positive Contact After” (red). The “No Contact Before” contact type is represented by a gray shaded bar. All bars are sorted from left to right based on the contact type.
